cluster_thesis.text: The memory supercycle itself is intact and arguably accelerating structurally (HBM wafer share of DRAM projected 18%->30% by end-2027, TrendForce 2027 HBM contract hikes guided +80-150%), but CXMT reaching HBM3E risk production ~1yr ahead of the 2027 consensus timeline (qualification-stage, shipping samples to Alibaba T-Head/Cambricon) introduces a genuine, dated competitive threat specifically to the HBM3-tier segment SK Hynix (SKHY) has near-monopolized and to MU's commodity-DRAM crowd-out thesis. Not yet in supplier pricing -- this is a WATCH on timing and magnitude, not a deteriorating call.
cluster_thesis.falsifier: CXMT HBM3E product actually enters a hyperscaler or ASIC-maker's qualified supplier list (beyond sampling to Alibaba T-Head/Cambricon), or a tier-1 source reports a first CXMT-linked HBM3E contract price -- either would move this from qualification-stage risk to realized ASP risk.

margin_pool.moving_toward: HBM (and within HBM, the newest qualified generation -- HBM4 Vera Rubin) as wafer allocation shifts from conventional DRAM into HBM (18%->30% of DRAM wafer input by end-2027)
margin_pool.moving_away_from: commodity DRAM margins get squeezed by the same crowd-out mechanism that is enriching HBM suppliers; WDC's HDD/nearline-storage margin pool is adjacent but structurally separate from both -- it is not migrating from or to the DRAM/HBM pool at all

evidence.claim: HBM wafer input rising from ~18% of total DRAM wafer input (end-2025) to ~30% (end-2027), the structural mechanism crowding out conventional DRAM
2027 HBM contract prices guided to 'surge multiples higher' (+80-150%)
~70% of Samsung's memory capacity locked under LTAs through 2031, meaning HBM3E spot spikes (4-5x LTA) accrue mainly to residual free capacity, not the pre-sold supplier base

differentiator_reads.axis: HBM4 sampling timing and committed capacity vs announced capacity
differentiator_reads.read: SK Hynix holds 60-70% of the HBM4 Vera Rubin supplier allocation, the largest and most concentrated share of the current ramp
strengthening thesis, rotation_bucket=accumulate, up +4.8% today despite carrying the same CXMT catalyst_threat trim as MU -- market pricing the threat as immaterial to the near-term HBM4 ramp

ranking.case_against: Highest beta in the entire 33-name book (2.442) and thinnest analyst coverage of the three (10 vs MU's 32); SK Hynix's HBM3E near-monopoly is precisely the generation CXMT is targeting, so a Chinese qualification success would first erode share at SK Hynix's stronghold tier, not at HBM4.

differentiator_reads.axis: DRAM vs NAND revenue mix, direction of each cycle independently
differentiator_reads.read: diversified DRAM (commodity+HBM) and NAND base gives MU exposure to two independent cycles, unlike SKHY's HBM-heavy concentration

differentiator_reads.axis: HBM4 sampling timing and committed capacity vs announced capacity
differentiator_reads.read: qualified for HBM4 Vera Rubin but allocation share is 'the remainder... realistically single digits to low teens' -- structurally thin on the fastest-inflecting tier
WATCH status is explicitly CXMT structural/capacity risk, not ASP -- CXMT reached HBM3E risk production ~1yr ahead of 2027 consensus, qualification-stage only

ranking.case_against: Largest analyst-target gap in the cluster (+51.3%, $1513.11 vs $1000.26) and today's PEER LEADER + TARGET GAP signal fires are real bullish evidence that argues for ranking MU above SKHY on pure upside, even while thesis stays at WATCH.

differentiator_reads.axis: enterprise SSD exposure as a separate AI-adjacent driver from DRAM
differentiator_reads.read: WDC completed its SanDisk (NAND/flash) spinoff in 2024 and is now a pure enterprise/nearline HDD maker -- it has no DRAM, HBM, or NAND revenue line at all, so this axis and the DRAM/NAND-mix axis both read as non-participant rather than exposed
WDC was not named in today's CXMT catalyst_threat trim alongside MU and SKHY -- consistent with WDC having no DRAM/HBM3-tier exposure for a domestic Chinese DRAM competitor to threaten

ranking.case_against: Best price mover in the cluster today (+2.1%), strengthening thesis, and the largest analyst-target gap in dollar terms among the three (+39.3%, $664.92 vs $477.30) -- on its own AI-storage-demand merits (nearline HDD capacity for AI training data) WDC's thesis is not weak, it is simply not the same trade as the DRAM/HBM tailwind this cluster question is about.

reorder_when: A tier-1 source reports a CXMT HBM3E product entering a real qualified-supplier list beyond Alibaba T-Head/Cambricon sampling, or a first CXMT-linked contract price appears -- would demote SKHY given SK Hynix's HBM3E concentration
SK Hynix's next quarterly print (expected late Oct 2026, exact date TBD) confirms or disappoints on HBM4 Vera Rubin allocation share -- direct read-through to both SKHY and MU
A tier-1, non-ratio-derived HBM3E contract-basis quote newer than 2026-01-15 appears (hbm_tracker G5), which would let ASP pass-through be judged directly rather than via the flat-within-basis proxy

redundant_pairs.same_bet_because: both are DRAM/HBM merchant memory suppliers riding the same HBM pricing tailwind

bench.why_better_than: offers pure-NAND exposure that none of the three held names provide cleanly (MU is mixed DRAM+NAND, WDC is HDD-only post-spinoff, SKHY is HBM-DRAM) -- was +11.9% on the 2026-09-04 memory-spike session, the largest single-day move of any name in that basket, and carries the highest ATR20 (15.6%) in the book's entire cache
bench.entry_condition: a pullback that confirms a base after its extreme volatility, or independent corroboration of the still-uncorroborated (hbm_tracker G8) DRAM +50%/NAND +60% QoQ Susquehanna report that drove the 09-04 spike

bench.why_better_than: captures Samsung + SK Hynix combined (>50% of the ETF's weight per hbm_tracker), the two largest HBM4 Vera Rubin allocation holders (25-30% + 60-70%), diversifying away SKHY's single-name beta (2.442, highest in the book) while keeping the same HBM4 tailwind
bench.entry_condition: no specific trigger identified this run -- a standing structural alternative for reducing single-name concentration risk within the HBM4 leadership bet

thesis_tensions.tension: Ranked laggard on the cluster's shared-tailwind question despite a strengthening per-name thesis and the best price move in the cluster today (+2.1%) -- the disagreement is structural (WDC is HDD-only post-SanDisk-spinoff, not a DRAM/HBM participant), not a quality judgment on WDC itself.

MU carries the cluster's single largest analyst-target upside (+51.3%) and fired PEER LEADER + TARGET GAP signals today, yet its thesis sits at WATCH (CXMT structural risk) and it is ranked below SKHY rather than above it -- upside on paper is not the same as capturing the fastest-inflecting part of the tailwind (HBM4 Vera Rubin), where MU is structurally thin.
